verdictStatement: All three claimed repairs land, and the central one is a real fix to a real gap that I missed at v6 and Codex caught. v7 adds machine.outcomeBranchDiscipline as a normative branch-selection algorithm with an explicit evaluation order, a mutual-exclusion claim, and a beforeFallback rule; it rewrites defaultTransition to apply that algorithm before any fallback and to state that fallback 'is not reachable for a named whenInactive case'; it retires the unqualified whenFailed on RECOVER-COMMIT in favour of whenActiveFailure carrying an explicit ACTIVE-but-other-conjunct-failed predicate; and it puts a normativeExclusion field on all three implicated fallbacks, each saying in terms 'This fallback MUST NOT supply the reason.' The discipline even anticipates the obvious objection with 'notesAreNotTheRule'. I worked the branch algebra by hand across every member and the routing is total and correct: INACTIVE yields ENVELOPE-INACTIVE at all five branched members, ACTIVE-with-guard yields acceptance, and ACTIVE-with-failure yields whenActiveFailure on RECOVER-COMMIT and the correct event fallback elsewhere. The roster now carries no narrowing parenthetical at all, closing the advisory Codex and I both raised. Codex v5 is pinned as a frozen COMPLETE REJECT and — importantly for my own v6 caveat — I read it and confirmed it carries exactly SITCV5-S1/S2 and nothing more, so the risk v6 booked never materialised and the now-empty notFoldedThisSuccessor is correct rather than convenient. Nothing regressed: every other block is byte-identical to v6, the vocabulary is still totally mapped, and the continuation table is unchanged. The single advisory is a precision gap in one sentence of the new algorithm.

advisories.title: whenInactive is the one branch the new discipline does not gate on the member's own applicability precondition
advisories.detail: outcomeBranchDiscipline says it applies to 'Any transitions[] member that names the (state, event) pair and declares one or more of' the branch objects, and defines whenInactive as 'true iff this member's TRUSTED-entry / envelope standing is INACTIVE'. The two ACTIVE branches are guard-gated by their own wording ('the member guard holds'), and branchless members are explicitly guard-gated. whenInactive is not. Four (state, event) pairs carry both a branched ordinary-payload member and the branchless recovery-staging member 6: ST-UNBOOTSTRAPPED, ST-EXPIRED, ST-STALE-REVOCATION and ST-QUORUM-LOST with EV-PRESENT-PAYLOAD. Read in isolation, a recovery-typed payload on one of those pairs while TRUSTED-entry is INACTIVE — which is the present state of the world — satisfies member 0/2's whenInactive as literally written, even though that member's guard begins 'Payload kind MUST be ordinary'.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The contract as a whole resolves it and resolves it the safe way. The member guard states the payload-kind precondition; airGapPayload.payloadKind.rule states independently that recovery payloads 'may only stage' and that 'A recovery payload NEVER enters ST-TRUSTED via EV-PRESENT-PAYLOAD'; and FC-PAYLOAD-KIND-DISJOINT, unchanged since v5, requires that a recovery-typed complete payload from ST-UNBOOTSTRAPPED stages and that 'The two guards are disjoint'. A harness built to the fixtures gets the intended behaviour. There is also no fail-open direction: the loose reading refuses where the correct reading stages, so the worst case is a liveness question about starting a ceremony, never an admission. And the artifact does not claim cross-member branch determinism anywhere, so no stated property is false — which is why I record this as precision rather than as a SHOULD-FIX.
advisories.suggestedFix: One clause in appliesTo: branches are evaluated only on a member whose applicability preconditions hold, payloadKind included; a member excluded by kind yields no branch and does not compete. That makes the discipline agree with payloadKind.rule and FC-PAYLOAD-KIND-DISJOINT explicitly instead of by inference.

repairVerification.algorithm: machine.outcomeBranchDiscipline is new and marked NORMATIVE. It declares an evaluationOrder of whenInactive, then whenActiveFailure, then whenActiveSuccess; a mutualExclusion rule; a branchlessMembers rule; and a beforeFallback rule stating that 'A named INACTIVE case therefore cannot emit PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE, INSTALL-NOT-TRUSTED, or RECOVERY-COMMIT-REFUSED.' It closes with 'notesAreNotTheRule', which answers Codex's objection that the v6 fallback notes merely asserted the outcome.
repairVerification.defaultTransition: Rewritten from v6's guard-first text to 'Apply outcomeBranchDiscipline first on every transitions[] member that names the (state, event) pair… It is not reachable for a named whenInactive case.' The attack 'defaultTransition still sending a false guard to fallback first' does not land.
repairVerification.whenFailedRetired: The whenFailed key is gone — zero occurrences as a key; the three surviving prose mentions all describe its retirement or are attack lines. Transition 16 now carries whenActiveFailure with an explicit predicate, 'TRUSTED-entry is ACTIVE and a recoveryTrustedEntry conjunct other than envelope standing fails', which is precisely the qualification Codex asked for.
repairVerification.normativeExclusion: All three implicated fallbacks gained a normativeExclusion field, each ending 'This fallback MUST NOT supply the reason.' EV-RECOVER-COMMIT's additionally distinguishes the ACTIVE-but-other-conjunct-failed case from a second reading of the fallback. EV-INSTALL's note — which Codex singled out as still claiming the ACTIVE precondition — is amended.
repairVerification.algebraWorkedByHand: I enumerated branches on every member. Five carry whenInactive and all five assign ENVELOPE-INACTIVE. Members 0–3 carry whenInactive plus whenActiveSuccess, so an ACTIVE guard failure yields no true branch and correctly reaches the event fallback for its own reason; member 16 carries all three and is closed without fallback. Every other member is branchless and guard-evaluated. The routing is total, and no INACTIVE case can reach a fallback reason.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed: That outcomeBranchDiscipline is prose rather than an algorithm. It declares standing NORMATIVE, an ordered branch list, a mutual-exclusion rule, a branchless rule and a fallback boundary — enough for a generated evaluator to choose without inventing precedence.
That retiring whenFailed left a dangling reference. The key is gone and every surviving mention describes the retirement.

That the ACTIVE-failure path lost its reason when whenActiveFailure was added only to member 16. It did not — members 0–3 correctly reach their own event fallback for an ACTIVE guard failure, which is what those fallback reasons exist for.
That the empty notFoldedThisSuccessor repeats the v4 defect. It does not — I read the now-frozen Codex v5 and confirmed there is nothing left to fold.
That some earlier repair regressed under the new discipline. Twenty-plus blocks compare byte-identical to v6 and the transitions differ only at index 16.
coordinatorNote: Two things worth recording. First, on calibration: Codex's SITCV6-S1 identified a genuine gap I missed when I accepted v6 — I verified that all five whenInactive branches carried ENVELOPE-INACTIVE but did not ask whether any rule sequenced those branches ahead of the guard-false fallback, which is exactly the question a conformance evaluator has to answer. v7 answers it properly, and I record the miss because it bears on how much weight a single reviewer's ACCEPT should carry on a machine this size. Second, my v6 ACCEPT was explicitly scope-limited because the Codex v5 verdict was unfrozen and off my permission list; that limit is now discharged. I read it, it carries exactly the two findings v6 folded, and no repair scope was missed — so the lineage does not have an unexamined gap behind it. The single advisory is one under-gated sentence in an otherwise careful new algorithm, it points in the refusing direction, and the behaviour it could confuse is already pinned by payloadKind.rule and an unchanged fixture. DR-112 remains OPEN, the subject remains CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED / DO-NOT-SEAL / binds NOTHING, and nothing here marks the row SATISFIED or authorizes docs/v2/implementation/.
